paper.title: MACE: Higher Order Equivariant Message Passing Neural Networks for Fast and Accurate Force Fields
paper.venue: 36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022)

problem_tree.node: Root: Development of fast and accurate force fields using higher order equivariant message passing neural networks.
problem_tree.description: The paper addresses the challenge of creating efficient and accurate interatomic potentials through the introduction of the MACE architecture, which utilizes higher order messages in message passing neural networks.

children.node: RQ1: How does the MACE architecture improve the efficiency of message passing in neural networks?
children.description: This question investigates the specific improvements in computational efficiency and scalability achieved by using higher order messages in the MACE architecture compared to traditional MPNNs.

children.task: Comparison of MACE with traditional MPNNs on benchmark tasks.
model_or_method: MACE architecture with higher order messages
metrics: Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) on energies and forces
children.protocol_or_setup: Two-layer MACE models with a local radial cutoff of 5 Å.
children.conclusion: MACE reduces the number of required message passing iterations to just two, improving computational efficiency.

children.node: RQ2: What are the effects of higher order messages on the learning curves of MACE?
children.description: This question explores how the inclusion of higher order messages influences the learning efficiency and accuracy of the MACE model.

children.task: Analysis of learning curves for MACE with varying correlation orders.
metrics: Learning curve steepness, RMSE on training data
children.protocol_or_setup: Training MACE models with correlation orders ν = 1, 2, 3.
children.conclusion: Higher order messages significantly improve the steepness of learning curves, indicating better data efficiency.

children.node: RQ3: How does MACE perform in terms of accuracy and computational cost compared to existing models?
children.description: This question assesses the performance of MACE in terms of accuracy on benchmark datasets and its computational efficiency compared to other state-of-the-art models.

children.task: Benchmarking MACE against other models on the rMD17 and 3BPA datasets.
metrics: Mean Absolute Error (MAE) on energies and forces, training time
children.protocol_or_setup: Training MACE models on specified datasets and comparing with BOTNet and NequIP.
children.conclusion: MACE achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while being significantly faster to train and evaluate than previous models.
